system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Headline points

1. **Do not accept the "FINAL / settled at principal level / market standard" framing.** The cover note says these positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened." Under playbook sections 0.4 and 6.3, that is a counterparty assertion, not an authority. We have no record of Amelia Frost giving written approval for any fallback in this draft. The "market context" preamble is advocacy and does not bind us. Our mark-up should say plainly that nothing is agreed until it is agreed in the long-form SPA.

2. **The 20% / AUD 4.8m cap is not cleared just because it matches our fallback number.** That fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given. It also comes packaged with thresholds, time limits and a collapse of the fundamental regime, which would make the cap worth far less than a 20% cap within our structure.

3. **The cover memo and the Disclosure Letter don't match.** On several points the Seller's own Disclosure Letter is more candid than its cover memo. It confirms that the Bluefen consent is not in hand, Riverlark is not repaid, the bonuses are excluded from the funds flow, and the incident is unresolved. We should use the Disclosure Letter's admissions to rebut the memo's characterisations ("addressed", "not material", "ordinary course", "adequate").

4. **The draft is stale.** The disclosure is "as at 22 September 2026." Today is 5 November 2026. Every factual item (Bluefen, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment status, DD-006 investigation, Sandbar renewals) must be refreshed. Any update must be distinguished as verified or merely asserted before we rely on it.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Liability architecture

| Item | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment / pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% only with written Amelia Frost authority (none) | **Reject; restate 25% / AUD 6m.** Do not signal the fallback. If the team wants to use it, escalate to Amelia Frost for written authority referencing this draft, and only as part of a package that fixes the items below. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** That is five times our position. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only (deductible) | AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar) | **Reject on both size and mechanism.** Combined with the AUD 25k de minimis, a AUD 250k deductible would screen out a large share of realistic claims. |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3/13)** | 18 months | 24 months; 18 is a fallback needing written approval (none) | **Reject; restate 24 months.** |
| **"Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Proposed | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | **Reject.** This is a hidden override. It would silently import the general cap, thresholds and time limits into indemnities, covenant claims, price/payment obligations, tax and title. Invert the default: general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly stated. |
| **Fundamental / Title** | Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | **Reject firmly.** Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we pay AUD 24m for. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap title at 20%. |
| **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)** | Proposed | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything, to the maximum extent enforceable; not waivable | **Reject.** As drafted this would purport to cap or bar claims for fraud and wilful concealment, and the non-reliance clause could be used against misrepresentation claims. Insert an express carve-out across cl 9.3, 12, 12.8 and 20.5 (and any time-bar clause). Also scope the exclusive remedy so it does not cut across specific indemnities, covenants, title or tax. |
| **Tax / IP** | "Settled under the general regime above" | OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | **Reject the characterisation.** Tax and IP are not settled. Our response should state they remain open and are not to be treated as falling within the general regime by default. We should not assert unlimited liability either. |

### B. Disclosure and knowledge

**General disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2; Schedule 7).** The Seller deems disclosed every matter in the data room, the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." This is exactly the whole-data-room and public-register disclosure the playbook rejects. Combined with the knowledge exclusion, it would largely hollow out the warranties.
- **Pushback:** delete 1.1 and 1.2. Only matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter count, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect, and against a specific warranty. Data-room documents may be referred to, but only specifically identified documents and only to the extent fairly disclosed.
- **Numbering gap:** the letter jumps from 1.2 to 1.4. Ask whether a paragraph 1.3 was deleted or exists in another version, and confirm the complete text.
- **Paragraph 1.4 (non-admission):** a non-admission statement is tolerable in principle. However, it must not be read as qualifying the warranties or as negating consent or payment obligations the SPA imposes. Add language that it does not limit the SPA's conditions, covenants or indemnities.

**Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3).** "No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records." This is a blanket exclusion that also deems constructive knowledge through "discoverable."
- **Pushback:** delete it. If any qualifier survives, it should cover only the actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals, and it must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity. Separately, Seller-side "awareness" qualifiers should be tied to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry.
- There is a further reason the clause is unacceptable. The specific indemnities we are seeking (e.g. Ironquay) exist precisely because we know about the issue. A knowledge bar would neutralise them.

### C. Deal-specific items

**Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3).** Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (around AUD 3.6m per DD-002), with change-control consent at cl 11.2 and conditions at 11.3. The Seller offers reasonable endeavours and "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent." Its own DL item 2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence the conditions are satisfied.
- **Pushback:** this should be a Condition Precedent requiring (i) an unconditional, effective written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2 that covers this transaction; and (ii) evidence satisfactory to the Buyer that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied or waived by Bluefen before Completion. A consent that is conditional or delivered but not yet effective does not satisfy the CP. Reasonable endeavours alone is not acceptable for a customer of this size. We need a Buyer-only waiver right and a long-stop date with a termination right. The memo's word "addressed" is not supported by the Seller's own letter.

**Riverlark (cl 2 / 7).** About AUD 3.2m outstanding (DD-003, change-control 8.1, discharge 9.2). The Seller offers a "release to be provided following Completion." DL item 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and there is no discharge.
- **Pushback:** require a current payout letter (refreshed close to Completion, with a per-diem amount), direct repayment from Completion funds, and executed, effective security releases and deeds of release (and PPSR discharge, if applicable) delivered at Completion. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's approval; we have neither. "Approximately" AUD 3.2m is not good enough for a debt-free price. We need the precise figure on the Completion date, and it must be deducted as Debt.

**Employee bonuses (funds flow / DD-005).** AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses is excluded from the funds flow. The memo calls them "a matter for the Seller." The letter (item 5) does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- **Pushback:** the payments are likely to be made by the Company, so the cost falls on us after Completion unless dealt with. Require either (a) a specific funds-flow line item treated as Debt or a Transaction Expense, covering the AUD 420k plus any triggered payroll tax, super, PAYG and on-costs; or (b) Seller funding with a specific indemnity. The words "a matter for the Seller" in a cover memo are not an operative mechanism. On-costs need to be quantified and not assumed to be nil.

**Ironquay IP (cl 11.1 / DD-004, DD-010).** The indemnity is limited to "the specific SOW3 payment." Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open. Per the playbook and DL item 4, that figure is not independently verified either way.
- **Pushback:** broaden the indemnity to cover any loss arising from the Company not owning, or being unable to freely use, the SOW3 Project Materials. That includes third-party claims, remediation and replacement costs, and any amounts Ironquay claims. Preserve the SOW3 cure: delivery before Completion of evidence of cleared payment plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay. Ask the Seller to verify the actual payment status. We should neither assume AUD 180k is owed nor assume it has been paid. The indemnity should not be capped at that figure and should sit outside the general cap, basket and knowledge bar.

**DD-006 export / privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sched 6).** The memo says it is "preliminary... not expected to be material." DL item 6 says a link was sent to an unintended external address, about 1,240 records may be affected, access, scope and notification are unknown, and the investigation is preliminary.
- **Pushback:** don't accept "not material," and don't overstate the position either. There is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure in either direction. Require covenants to (i) preserve all logs and evidence; (ii) complete the investigation, including access logs, link expiry and recipient contact; (iii) give the Buyer regular updates and consultation rights before any regulatory or affected-person communication; and (iv) provide a specific warranty or indemnity for loss arising from the incident, outside the general limitations and disclosure. Seek a refreshed status, since six-plus weeks have passed.

**Sandbar renewals (DD-008, DD-011; AUD 330,000).** The memo asserts these are "ordinary-course operating costs." DL item 8 says they should be read together, and that the letter does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Pushback:** reserve our position. Request the contracts, timing, termination rights and whether amounts are prepaid or accrued, and whether the renewals were entered in the ordinary course and in compliance with any interim-period covenants. Per the playbook, we should **not** pre-emptively treat them as Debt or demand a price deduction. The outcome depends on that analysis.

**Title (DD-012).** The Seller relies solely on the Company's own share register.
- **Pushback:** the register is an internally supplied source, not independent proof. Require an ASIC company extract, PPSR searches against the Seller and the Company for security over the shares, evidence of the Seller's capacity and authority (board resolution and, if relevant, any trustee or constitution authority), share certificates, confirmation of no options or convertibles, and a release of any encumbrance (including any Riverlark share security). Title warranties belong in the fundamental regime (see section A).

**Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The letter says the lease has a notification obligation only, and that Mossvale's assignment restriction is not triggered by a share sale. These are Seller characterisations.
- **Pushback:** our counsel should review both clauses directly, including any change-of-control language or deemed-assignment definitions. If only notification applies, add a completion deliverable or covenant to give the notice.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Reject outright**
1. The "FINAL / agreed / market standard / settled at principal level" framing. State expressly that nothing is agreed.
2. Fundamental and title claims sharing the general cap and time limits.
3. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature." Insert a full fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out.
4. The "any limitation applies to all Claims" default (a hidden general-regime override).
5. General data-room, public-register and Accounts disclosure (DL 1.1–1.2).
6. The blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion, including "discoverable" (cl 8.3).

**Restate our starting positions**
7. Cap of 25% / AUD 6.0m.
8. De minimis of AUD 5k and a tipping basket of AUD 50k.
9. General claims period of 24 months.
10. Fundamental and title regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside thresholds and the knowledge bar.
11. Tax and IP: OPEN, not settled under the general regime.

**Deal-specific mechanics**
12. Bluefen: CP requiring effective consent plus evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion, with a Buyer-only waiver and long-stop/termination right.
13. Riverlark: current payout letter, repayment directly from Completion funds, effective releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
14. Bonuses: AUD 420k plus quantified on-costs as a funds-flow line item (Debt/Transaction Expense) or Seller-funded with an indemnity.
15. Ironquay: broadened indemnity outside the general limits, with the SOW3 cure (cleared payment evidence plus confirmatory assignment) preserved. The AUD 180k is to be verified, not assumed.
16. DD-006: preservation, investigation, update and consultation covenants plus a specific protection. No assumptions about breach, notification or loss.
17. Sandbar: information request and analysis. No automatic Debt classification.
18. Title: independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, authority, certificates, encumbrance releases).
19. Lease and Mossvale: independent review of the clauses, and a notice deliverable where needed.

**Process and authority**
20. **Escalate to Amelia Frost** before anyone mentions or concedes the 20% cap or the 18-month period. If she is minded to authorise either, it should be in writing, identify this draft, and ideally be tied to the Seller conceding the structural points (items 2–6).
21. **Refresh all facts** from 22 September 2026 to now. Require a brought-down Disclosure Letter, and treat any Seller update as an assertion until verified.
22. **Complete the document** by asking for the missing DL paragraph 1.3 and the full clause text of the SPA sections referenced (we only have summaries, so drafting-level review is still needed).

I can prepare a short cover email to Seller's counsel and a draft escalation note to Amelia Frost if that would help.
=== END ADVICE ===
